title: Tech 04 Token Rotation
decision: Choose an authentication-token rotation strategy with legacy-client constraints.
context: The service issues signed access tokens to web, mobile, and embedded clients.
A signing key must be rotated because its handling process is being replaced.
constraints: No forced logout for more than 2 percent of active users.
The old key must stop signing immediately.
Verification support for the old key may continue temporarily.
options: Replace the key immediately and verify only the new key.
Start signing with the new key while temporarily verifying both old and new keys.
Continue signing with the old key until every legacy client updates.

evidence.fact: Access tokens expire after 45 minutes and refresh tokens are validated server-side.
About 1.4 percent of weekly active clients are on versions more than 90 days old.
All deployed services can load two verification keys without a restart.
Security policy permits a maximum 24-hour overlap for verification keys during planned rotation.
The old private key can be disabled for signing independently of keeping its public verification material.
Client token verification is performed by services using server-published public keys rather than by embedding signing keys in clients.
